question: Zoom in on the 2023 season: give me Red Bull's headline numbers, and show how championship points compare with race wins for the top 10 drivers.

recorded.note: Verbatim DinoAI output for a follow-up in the same session. KPI values and chart rows match the warehouse. The prose has two slips the data does not support ('23 of the 22 races', and seven of the top 10 drivers had no win, not six); they are kept to show why the Data tab matters. The delay is approximate.

turn.content:
Red Bull dominated the 2023 season, winning 21 of 22 races (a 95% win rate) and clinching the constructors' title with 860 points. Max Verstappen alone accounted for 19 of those wins and nearly doubled his teammate's points total.

- Max Verstappen won 19 of 22 races and scored more than double the points of any other driver on the grid.
- Sergio Pérez's 2 wins and 285 points were enough for 2nd overall, but nowhere close to his teammate.
- Six of the top 10 drivers — including Hamilton, Alonso, Leclerc, Norris, Russell and Stroll — finished the season without a single win, relying entirely on podiums and points-paying finishes.
- Red Bull's two drivers combined for 23 of the 22 races counted as wins across the season (21 team wins, split 19-2), effectively locking out the win column for every other constructor almost all year.

Assumptions: "Championship points" is each driver's cumulative points total at season end; "race wins" counts 1st-place finishes only; DNF means the driver did not finish the race.
